findings.invariant: The actual year-4000 input is either representable and roundtrips, or specifically rejected as unrepresentable on the native platform.
findings.finding: The 2^40 os.date probe is only the upstream branch selector. Neither successful nor rejected probe tests os.time{year=4000,month=1,day=1}; range-error recovery at an ordinary year does not establish that assertion.
findings.required_change: Exercise actual year4000 with native C and Ada, requiring its exact representability rejection or date/instant roundtrip according to native support. Preserve separately reviewed native maximum/next-second boundary pair and huge-time rejection obligations.

findings.invariant: Removing isdst from a native date table preserves the original represented instant.
findings.finding: Each omitted/false/true case self-roundtrips its own resulting instant, so an incorrect omitted-DST default can produce a different instant and still pass. This is weaker than upstream t==t1.
findings.required_change: Save os.time of an actual native date table, clear its isdst, and assert the resulting instant equals the saved instant. Retain explicit true/false normalization as supplemental coverage and report native output-field presence.

findings.invariant: Out-of-C-int date fields fail during field conversion with the correct field-specific out-of-bound diagnostic.
findings.finding: rejected accepts either out-of-bound or represented for every operation. Thus a failure to enforce the year/day/month field boundary could fall through to mktime representation failure and still pass.
findings.required_change: Parameterize required diagnostic; require field year/day/month out-of-bound for those respective probes and cannot-be-represented for representation-only probes. Shared recovery can remain supplemental.

evidence_review.observed: Cint4/LuaInteger8; 2^40 representation rejection; boolean isdst. These facts do not establish the missing assertions.
